Article Title: In 1982, a Minnesota farmer wrote a will leaving his 300-acre farm to his son after his wife's lifetime; a different 1989 will later emerged, and a 2026 appeals court reversed the reopening of his est
Article Text:
A second will emerges years after the farmer's death

Why the appeals court reversed the decision

Finality of inheritance decisions at stake

A Minnesota inheritance dispute over a 300-acre farm has taken another turn after an appeals court reversed a lower court's decision to reopen a deceased farmer's estate, years after a second will surfaced. In a September 8, 2026, ruling, the Minnesota Court of Appeals held that a court's failure to meet a statutory requirement for medical-assistance claims clearance did not deprive it of the authority to decide the estate case. The decision restored the legal standing of a 2017 property decree that had been set aside, according to the court's published opinion in In re the Estate of Clarence Vatthauer.The case centres on two wills signed by Clarence Vatthauer, who owned and farmed approximately 300 acres of productive farmland and cattle pasture in Red Lake County, Minnesota. His 1982 will gave his wife, Fern Vatthauer, the right to use the property during her lifetime, with the remainder passing to their son, David Vatthauer. A second will, executed in 1989, revoked the earlier document and left the land to Fern outright. The competing documents eventually triggered a family dispute over who was entitled to inherit the property.Clarence died in 2005. In 2015, David petitioned the district court to distribute his father's estate and submitted the 1982 will.The court issued a decree of descent in 2017, establishing property ownership according to that document. At the time, the record did not indicate that any family member knew about the later will. David had also not filed a clearance for medical-assistance claims against his father's estate, a statutory requirement for a court to issue a decree of descent.The dispute resurfaced after Clarence's daughter, Julie Ford, was appointed guardian of Fern in 2022 as her health declined. Ford contacted the law firm that had handled her parents' estate planning and discovered the 1989 wills executed by both Clarence and Fern. Clarence's later will changed the inheritance arrangement substantially. Instead of giving Fern a lifetime interest followed by ownership passing to David, it gave her the farm outright. Fern's own 1989 will directed that her property be distributed equally among her children.Ford sought to have the earlier decree vacated and Clarence's 1989 will admitted to probate. She argued that the 2017 decree was void because the court had issued it without the required clearance for medical-assistance claims. She also argued that exceptional circumstances justified reopening the case.Fern died in October 2023. The district court subsequently ordered the two 1989 wills probated, vacated the 2017 decree and ruled that the farm had passed to Fern outright before being distributed equally among her surviving children under her will.David challenged the lower court's decision, arguing that the failure to obtain the clearance did not strip the court of subject-matter jurisdiction, or its legal authority to hear and decide the type of case involved. The Minnesota Court of Appeals agreed with him. In its September 2026 opinion, the court acknowledged that the district court had violated the statutory requirement. However, it drew a distinction between making a legal or procedural error and lacking the jurisdiction to decide a case.Minnesota law grants district courts broad jurisdiction over matters relating to deceased people's estates. Although state law requires medical-assistance claims to be cleared or resolved before a decree of descent is entered, the appeals court found no clear legislative statement that violating this requirement removes a court's subject-matter jurisdiction.The judges therefore concluded that the 2017 decree was not automatically void simply because the required clearance had not been filed. The legal error could have been challenged through the appropriate correction or appeal procedures, but the ordinary appeal period had expired years before the lower court attempted to vacate the decree.The appeals court also rejected the argument that the case should be sent back for the district court to reconsider whether exceptional circumstances justified reopening it. It said the relevant procedural rule did not provide a mechanism for correcting the type of judicial error involved.The ruling highlights a broader legal principle: courts must balance the need to correct mistakes against the need for finality in inheritance proceedings. The appeals court noted that allowing a final estate decree to be challenged years later on the basis of a legal error could leave property ownership uncertain long after an estate had been distributed.The judges referred to Minnesota's probate code, which aims to provide an efficient process for settling estates and distributing property to successors. They also cited established precedent emphasising that parties generally must use the prescribed appeal process to challenge a court's decision rather than reopen it indefinitely.The case was reversed and remanded, meaning it was sent back to the district court for further orders consistent with the appeals court's ruling. The lower court must recognise that it improperly vacated the 2017 decree and that the decree became final when no party appealed it within the required period.The decision does not mean the appeals court found that the 1982 will was necessarily the last valid will. Instead, it held that the lower court could not invalidate the earlier decree on the jurisdictional grounds it had relied upon.
Article Summary: The case centres on two wills signed by Clarence Vatthauer, who owned and farmed approximately 300 acres of productive farmland and cattle pasture in Red Lake County, Minnesota. His 1982 will gave his wife, Fern, the right to use the property during her lifetime, with the remainder passing to their son, David. A second will, executed in 1989, revoked the earlier document and left the land to Fern outright. The competing documents eventually triggered a family dispute over who was entitled to inherit the property.

Article Title: “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to…”: Elon Musk’s proposed $10.6 billion giveaway could reach 72 million young people in America; but who will qualify
Article Text:
Elon Musk plans to give every American child a SpaceX share in 2027

SpaceX shares could put Musk's proposed giveaway at $10.6 billion

Anthropic's public benefit fund preceded the announcement

Elon Musk's SpaceX pledge raises questions over Trump Accounts

Elon Musk's SpaceX giveaway plan leaves transfer details unresolved

Elon Musk has announced plans to give every child in America a share of SpaceX in 2027, a proposal that could involve tens of millions of recipients and billions of dollars in stock. The pledge came hours after the billionaire criticised artificial intelligence company Anthropic for planning to place part of its equity in a public benefit fund, suggesting instead that shares should go directly to people. Musk has not explained who would qualify, how the transfers would work or whether the plan would use existing investment accounts for children. According to a Forbes report, based on current estimates, the proposed giveaway could involve around 72 million young people.In the X (formerly Twitter) post on October 19, Musk said he would give one of his SpaceX shares to every American child in 2027, describing the proposed distribution as the first of several such initiatives. He did not set out a timetable or explain whether the offer would cover all children living in the country or only those meeting particular eligibility requirements.Forbes reported, the US Census Bureau estimated that about 21.1% of the country's 341.8 million residents were children, equivalent to roughly 72.1 million people.That figure includes citizens and non-citizens, and Musk has not clarified whether his pledge would extend to both groups.There is also no published explanation of how the shares would reach their intended recipients. The announcement does not establish whether parents would need to register their children, whether the stock would be held in dedicated accounts or whether any restrictions would apply to the eventual sale of the shares.The financial scale of the pledge depends on the number of children who qualify and the value of SpaceX stock when the transfers take place. Using the Census Bureau's estimate of approximately 72.1 million people under 18 and the reported premarket share price of $147.52 on October 19, the total value would come to around $10.6 billion if each child received one share at that price.That calculation is an estimate, not a confirmed valuation of the proposed giveaway. SpaceX shares can change in value, and the number of eligible recipients has not been established. The final cost would also depend on the arrangements used to distribute the stock.Musk's personal holdings appear large enough to accommodate a transfer of this size, based on figures disclosed earlier in the year. As reported by Forbes, an SEC filing, an August filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission reported that he held 6.42 billion SpaceX shares as of June 30. The figure included stock held through trusts for which he serves as trustee, restricted shares and shares issuable through options.A distribution of 72 million shares would represent slightly more than 1% of that reported total.The pledge followed a separate announcement by Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence chatbot. On October 18, the company said it would commit at least 5% of its shares to a newly established Anthropic Public Benefit Fund.The proposed fund is intended to support charitable organisations and could also make direct distributions to selected groups of people. Anthropic described it as a wholly owned limited liability company, setting out a structure through which the company could direct resources towards public benefit activities. Musk responded to the announcement on X, “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public.”The US government's Trump Accounts programme could provide relevant context for Musk's proposal, although he has not said whether his plan is connected to it. Earlier in 2026, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged to contribute one SpaceX share each to the accounts of more than two million American children under the programme. The initiative provides a framework for holding investments on behalf of young people.The proposed distribution would come from a company in which Musk has a significant financial interest. Forbes estimated his net worth at $908.5 billion in its October 19 report, placing him at the top of its real-time billionaire rankings. His wealth is closely tied to his business holdings, including SpaceX and Tesla.The report also noted that SpaceX shares rose by more than 1% to $147.52 in premarket trading that Monday, alongside a broader recovery in US stock futures following the previous week's market losses. The quoted price provides a reference point for estimating the possible value of the giveaway, but it does not establish what the shares would be worth when they are distributed.
Article Summary: Elon Musk plans to give every American child a SpaceX share in 2027. The billionaire has not explained who would qualify, how the transfers would work or whether the plan would use existing investment accounts for children. The pledge came hours after the billionaire criticised artificial intelligence company Anthropic for planning to place part of its equity in a public benefit fund.

Article Title: 'Canada took advantage of US, but we're getting close to a deal': Trump claims 'no rush' to resume talks
Article Text:
Donald Trump has voiced concerns that Canada has been exploiting trade advantages over the United States for years. (Pic Credit: AP)

Trump says he is in no hurry to resume trade talks

Trump alleges imbalance in US-Canada trade

US president Donald Trump has accused Canada of taking advantage of the United States through trade imbalances over several years, while expressing confidence that the two countries could eventually reach an agreement that benefits the American economy.Speaking to FOX 2’s Roop Raj ahead of a rally in Michigan, Trump claimed Canada had earned billions of dollars annually at the expense of the US. However, he said discussions between the neighbouring countries were moving towards a possible resolution, according to the news agency ANI.“Canada has been making $90B/year off us for years and years. They've taken advantage of our country, but we're getting close to a deal... I love Canada; I love everything about it - other than some of the leaders,” Trump said.The US President also stressed that he was seeking a lasting agreement rather than a temporary arrangement, arguing that the final deal should deliver long-term economic benefits for the country.“I want to make the right deal. I'm not a short-term person, I'm a long-term. When the deal is made, it'll be a great deal for America,” he added.Earlier this month, Trump said he was in no rush to restart trade negotiations with Canada, accusing Ottawa of treating Washington unfairly. He also insisted that Canada would have to act honestly for any future agreement to move forward.Asked whether negotiations would resume before the US midterm elections, Trump offered no timeline and questioned Canada's conduct in its trade relationship with the US.“I don't know. Canada behaves very badly with the United States and I don't know,” he said.Trump further alleged that Washington had discovered Canadian tariffs that he claimed had previously gone unnoticed by others. However, he did not specify which tariffs he was referring to.“We caught them in the act; they charged us a lot of tariffs that nobody knew about except me. And it will work out eventually, but I don't know about I'm in no rush,” he said.His remarks indicated that an early resumption of talks was not a priority, although he maintained that the dispute could eventually be resolved.Trump reiterated his criticism of the commercial relationship between the two countries, claiming that Canada benefited disproportionately from its economic ties with the United States.“You know, Canada does all their business with us, we do very little business with them,” he said.He also argued that Canada needed to demonstrate greater transparency and fairness in its dealings with Washington.“And all we ask of one thing in Canada, they have to be honest. They are not honest with the United States; they've been ripping us off for years,” Trump added.Despite his criticism of Canadian leaders and trade practices, Trump expressed optimism that a future agreement could resolve the dispute. He did not provide further details about the proposed deal or indicate when negotiations might be concluded.
Article Summary: Donald Trump says he is in no hurry to resume trade talks with Canada. Claims Canada has been taking advantage of the United States for years. Insists he is seeking a long-term deal that benefits the American economy. However, offers no timeline for resumption of talks.

Article Title: US has ‘two very different sets of intelligence reports’: Trump rules out Sunday strikes on Iran
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump ruled out immediate military strikes against Iran on Sunday

Trump claims US controls Strait of Hormuz

Trump signals Russia-Ukraine peace talks

Trump links European unrest to immigration

Trump accuses Taiwan of taking US chip industry

US President Donald Trump on Sunday ruled out an immediate military strike against Iran, saying Washington had no plans to launch an attack that day, even as conflicting intelligence assessments and uncertainty over diplomatic efforts continued to shape the US approach to Tehran."Would I tell you that? But the answer is no. There will not be a strike," Trump told reporters as he departed the White House for a campaign rally in Michigan, responding to a question about whether military action against Iran could take place as soon as Sunday."We have two very different sets of intelligence reports," Trump said, describing the incoming information as "very advanced."The president maintained that Washington was doing "well with Iran," although an unnamed US official told Israeli news channel i24NEWS that Trump was prepared to "shift gears on Iran" and that military strikes no longer appeared to be "a question of if, but of when."The remarks came after Trump presented Tehran with a stark choice between reaching a diplomatic agreement and facing further military action."Do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off? That's the only question," Trump told Fox News, framing the next phase of the conflict as a choice between negotiations and escalating military operations.Despite ruling out a strike on Sunday, Trump has continued to signal that Washington could pursue further military action if negotiations fail to produce an agreement.Trump also asserted that American forces had established maritime dominance over the Strait of Hormuz, a key global shipping route and a major point of contention in the conflict with Iran."Remember, we now control the Hormuz Strait. They get nothing. Yes, we get everything." He maintained that commercial activity through the chokepoint had exceeded pre-war levels and described the US Navy's enforcement of a blockade on Iranian ports and shipping as "unbelievable."On Saturday, Trump had suggested that Washington could either launch fresh military strikes or secure a comprehensive agreement with Tehran. He questioned whether Iran would honour any commitments under a potential deal, while arguing that either outcome would amount to an American victory.Control over the Strait of Hormuz remains a central point of friction in the conflict, which erupted in late February following joint US-Israeli strikes. The confrontation has continued despite a ceasefire and a memorandum aimed at securing a final peace agreement.Turning to the war in Eastern Europe, Trump indicated that high-level diplomatic engagements involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine could take place soon."We're going to be having some pretty soon, and I think they both want to make a deal," he said, expressing optimism about the prospects of negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv.Trump did not provide further details about the proposed engagements or specify when the talks would take place.On Brazil's presidential election, the US president refrained from endorsing either candidate, saying his administration was "watching" the race.Trump also criticised immigration policies in European countries, linking protests and unrest in France, Italy, Belgium and Spain to what he described as inadequate border enforcement.Contrasting the situation in Europe with US border controls, he claimed that the United States had prevented unauthorised crossings over the preceding 18 months."I closed the border. You know that we've had zero infiltration," Trump said, asserting that "zero illegal aliens" had entered the country during that period. He also claimed that previous US administrations had allowed millions of people to enter illegally.Referring to his conversations with French President Emmanuel Macron, Trump said he had previously warned the French leader about the consequences of immigration policies."'You are destroying France. You're letting people come in that hate your country.'" Trump said he had told Macron.He also cited migrant arrivals in Spain as evidence of what he described as wider instability across Europe.On semiconductor manufacturing and trade, Trump accused Taiwan of taking over the US chip industry through low-cost production, renewing his criticism of the island's position in the global semiconductor supply chain."They stole our chip business, all of it, 100%, because they made chips at a ridiculous price, and they just pushed them in," Trump said.He argued that stronger executive leadership in Washington could have prevented broader tensions with China over trade and technology.Trump's comments come amid continuing US efforts to strengthen domestic semiconductor manufacturing and address Washington's strategic competition with Beijing.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump ruled out an immediate military strike against Iran on Sunday. He said Washington had no plans to launch an attack that day, even as conflicting intelligence assessments and uncertainty over diplomatic efforts continued to shape the US approach to Tehran. Trump indicated that high-level diplomatic engagements involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine could take place soon.

Article Title: ‘Vote for Netanyahu’: Trump urges Israelis to re-elect ‘outstanding warrior’ PM to ‘finish job’ in Iran
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump, right, poses for a photo with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

US President Donald Trump has urged Israelis to vote for the return of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to office, saying that the two leaders must “finish the job” against Iran.The appeal came on Sunday, two days before the election, as polls show Netanyahu’s coalition is far short of a majority. In a fresh post on Truth Social, Trump renewed his endorsement of Netanyahu, whom he first backed a week ago. The latest intervention comes after an Axios report that the Israeli prime minister had been pushing the US president to publicly reaffirm his support.The US President wrote, “To the people of Israel, to those who haven’t seen it, I am attaching the Endorsement I gave one week ago to your Prime Minister, Bibi Netanyahu. As everyone is aware, including the enemy, Bibi and I have had a great relationship in winning together.”Trump also linked his appeal directly to the military campaign against Iran, presenting his cooperation with Netanyahu as a shared effort and urging Israelis to consider what he described as the prime minister’s record as an “outstanding Warrior Prime Minister.”“I did the Venezuelan attack, one of the most successful Military Operations in History but, before that, we did Operation Midnight Hammer, stopping the World’s Number One State Sponsor of Terror from obtaining a Nuclear Weapon.Then we did Operation Epic Fury, and Iran now has No Navy, No Air Force, and both their Military and Economy are in shambles, including the fact that Iran’s Inflation is at 301%. The Naval Blockade has precluded them from getting Oil, and two levels of leadership, both Military and otherwise, are gone. When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister!Trump urged Israelis to re-elect Netanyahu, saying the two leaders must continue their campaign against Iran and prevent threats to Israel and the US. “Israel was called The Little Satan, with the United States being called The Big Satan, by some very evil people. There can no longer be the chant heard around the World of “Death to America, Death to Israel,” and there won’t be. Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started! President DONALD J TRUMP”Trump’s latest show of support comes after months of reported differences over the handling of the conflict with Iran. Many media reports had portrayed the US president as frustrated with Netanyahu for allegedly promising a quick victory against Tehran at the start of the year, a result that did not eventually materialise.The relationship also faced reported strains when Washington chose to halt its campaign against Iran and pursue an agreement. Israel was wary that a deal between the sides could undermine its security.Back in June, Israel’s continued strikes in Lebanon frustrated peace talks with Iran, prompting expletive-laden criticism of Netanyahu from Trump. The US president said then that he would “most likely” endorse Netanyahu’s re-election bid, but wanted to see who else was running before making a decision.Despite these reported disagreements, both leaders have continued to insist that they have a good working relationship.Trump has also repeatedly spoke about elections in other countries, departing from the longstanding norm that US presidents do not publicly intervene in the electoral contests of allied nations.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has urged Israelis to vote for the return of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to office. The appeal came on Sunday, two days before the election, as polls show Netanyahu’s coalition is far short of a majority. In a fresh post on Truth Social, Trump renewed his endorsement of Netanyahu, whom he first backed a week ago.

Article Title: Did US officials campaign to tilt Brazil polls towards Bolsonaros?
Article Text: Two US state department officials led a campaign to restore Brazil’s right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power and pushed sanctions intended to tilt the presidential election in its favour, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Senator Flavio Bolsonaro was facing leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off Sunday.The officials were Darren Beattie, senior adviser for Western Hemisphere Affairs overseeing Brazil policy, and Ricardo Pita, another senior adviser promoted this year to deputy assistant secretary for North America. Reuters could not determine whether they acted on orders from White House or secretary of state Marco Rubio. President Trump, a defender of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has not publicly endorsed any Brazilian candidate.Before campaigning began, Beattie and Pita told US diplomats that Washington’s policy was to restore Jair Bolsonaro as Brazil’s leader, although he had been disqualified from office for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to Lula, three sources said. After Bolsonaro received a 27-year sentence in Sept 2025, they shifted support to his son Flavio and instructed embassy staff not to engage with rival conservative contenders, the sources said.Since last year, the officials have advocated punitive measures designed to weaken Lula and boost the Bolsonaros, the 10 sources said. These included designating Brazil’s leading gangs, Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV), as terrorist organisations and sanctioning Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led investigations into Jair Bolsonaro.State department spokesman Tommy Pigott did not address questions about Beattie and Pita but said: “All actions taken by US against narco-traffickers and to protect free speech are to defend the rights and lives of the American people. The Brazilian people have the right to choose their leaders through free and fair elections.” White House declined to comment, while Lula’s office did not respond to requests.Orna Blum, who led state department’s Brazil and Southern Cone office until retiring last year over opposition to Trump administration, said Washington had the right to pursue its interests but added: “But when American foreign policy instruments are used to pressure another democracy over the legal fate of a political ally, the line between diplomacy and political intervention has been crossed.”Beattie is a former White House speechwriter fired in 2018 after addressing an event frequented by white nationalists. He developed “free speech diplomacy”, aimed at punishing countries accused of censoring right-wing speech. Washington accused Moraes of violating free-speech rights by jailing Brazilians over political social-media posts and censoring US platforms. Moraes, who did not respond to Reuters, has said he was combating fake news that undermined faith in democratic institutions.In early 2025, the Bolsonaro family lobbied for sanctions against Moraes under Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act. Jair Bolsonaro’s younger son Eduardo visited Beattie in Washington around April, two former officials said. Beattie then appealed to treasury department’s office of foreign assets control for sanctions, a former official said. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent offered no opposition, the official said. Sanctions were imposed in July 2025 over alleged free-speech violations.Pita also asked sanctions officials to explore terrorist designations for PCC and CV after joining a US delegation that visited Jair Bolsonaro in Brasilia in May 2025. In May 2026, Flavio met Beattie and deputy secretary of state Christopher Landau in Washington to discuss the designations. State department announced them the next day, though Reuters could not establish Beattie or Pita’s influence on the final decision.In July 2025, Washington revoked eight Supreme Court justices’ visas and imposed 50% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing Bolsonaro’s “persecution”. Analysts said court measures failed to stop his trial and tariffs boosted Lula’s ratings. Washington later diluted tariffs, removed Moraes from sanctions list in December and Brazil barred Beattie from visiting Bolsonaro in prison in March. Trump called Flavio’s narrow first-round lead over Lula a “big victory”.
Article Summary: Two US state department officials led a campaign to restore Brazil’s right-wing Bolsonaro clan to power. Darren Beattie and Ricardo Pita pushed sanctions intended to tilt the presidential election in its favour, according to 10 current and former US officials with direct knowledge of the matter. Senator Flavio Bolsonario was facing leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a tight run-off.

Article Title: A Texas billionaire couple bought a 40,000-acre Nebraska ranch for $56 million; the property has a history of prominent owners, and its new owners want to build a major cattle operation
Article Text:
PC: Nebraska Examiner

What makes the $56 million Nebraska ranch ideal for cattle production

PC; Nebraska Examiner

What is the history of Nebraska’s Pawnee Springs Ranch

What are the new owners’ plans for Pawnee Springs Ranch

How did Mark and Robyn Jones build their $2 billion fortune

A Texas billionaire couple has bought a roughly 40,000-acre Nebraska ranch for $56 million, in what appears to be a record-high ranch sale in the state. Mark and Robyn Jones, founders of insurance brokerage Goosehead Insurance, acquired Pawnee Springs Ranch in Lincoln County, a property with a history of prominent owners, including former Nebraska governor Keith Neville and businessman Peter Kiewit. According to the Nebraska Examiner, the couple plans to maintain the ranch’s existing cattle and agricultural operations while developing a “world-class cattle operation” over several years. The purchase also reflects their wider investment interests, with plans to explore further acquisitions across Nebraska, Kansas, Wyoming and Montana.Pawnee Springs Ranch is located in Lincoln County, east of North Platte, and extends from the North Platte River north into Nebraska's Sandhills. The property has nearly six miles of river frontage, nine centre pivots covering approximately 1,700 irrigated acres, calf backgrounding facilities with concrete feed bunks and an indoor-outdoor arena. Its landscape includes fertile river-bottom land and native Sandhills rangeland, which also provides habitat for deer, turkey and waterfowl.Mark Johnson of Hall and Hall, the agricultural real estate company that represented both parties in the transaction, described the property as exemplifying the top qualities of a Nebraska Sandhills river ranch.The ranch already has approximately 2,500 mother cows, alongside its irrigation infrastructure, grassland and river corridors. Mark Jones told the Nebraska Examiner that he wanted an operation focused on “actual agricultural production”, with the property's existing resources supporting the couple's plans for beef production.Pawnee Springs Ranch has a history dating back to 1918, and its previous owners include former Nebraska governor Keith Neville and construction businessman Peter Kiewit. Kiewit purchased the operation in 1949. He once told the North Platte Telegraph that the ranch took its name from the natural springs that flowed through the area.The Gottsch family became involved with the ranch in 1985, initially leasing the property before eventually purchasing it. The family subsequently operated it as part of its wider agricultural business, which has interests across Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri and Texas. In a statement following the sale, the Gottsches said the ranch had been part of their family for 41 years and recalled three generations participating in spring branding, summer grazing and autumn and winter calf backgrounding. They also thanked the Boeshart family caretakers and neighbouring ranchers who helped during branding season.The new owners intend to retain the ranch's existing agricultural activities while building a larger beef production business over several years. Ryan Langston, Mark Jones's son-in-law and the ranch's new chief executive, said the property would largely continue its current work, including raising calves from birth until weaning and returning them to grass as yearlings. The operation will also continue running its agricultural irrigation pivots.The transition will include retaining the three cowboys who currently live and work on the property. Langston said a new manager would be recruited to replace the existing manager, who is leaving with the Gottsch family. He also described the purchase as a “long-term commitment to the area” and said the owners intended to hire local workers where possible, work with neighbouring landowners and contribute to the local community. The couple does not plan to live in Nebraska but expects to maintain an active presence in the area.Mark and Robyn Jones built their fortune through their involvement in Goosehead Insurance, the publicly traded insurance brokerage they founded and developed together. The company connects customers with providers of home, motor, flood and other insurance products. The couple continues to serve as its chair and vice-chair, respectively. Forbes estimated their combined net worth at $2 billion, with Robyn Jones also appearing on its 2025 list of America's richest self-made women entrepreneurs.The Nebraska purchase follows their acquisition of Flathead Ridge Ranch in Montana in 2021, a 125,000-acre property that the couple describes as a family legacy investment. Their approach to that ranch has focused on conservation, forest restoration and maintaining public recreational access across most of the property. By contrast, Pawnee Springs Ranch is intended to serve as a commercial agricultural enterprise. Mark Jones told the Nebraska Examiner that the Nebraska operation “will be a platform we can build on”, with the couple looking towards further investments in Nebraska, Kansas, Wyoming and Montana. He also said the opportunity for their grandchildren to work on the ranch was an important attraction of the purchase.
Article Summary: Pawnee Springs Ranch is located in Lincoln County, east of North Platte. The property has nearly six miles of river frontage, nine centre pivots covering approximately 1,700 irrigated acres, calf backgrounding facilities with concrete feed bunks and an indoor-outdoor arena. Previous owners include former Nebraska governor Keith Neville and businessman Peter Kiewit. Mark and Robyn Jones built their fortune through their involvement in Goosehead Insurance.

Article Title: Obama unloads on Trump while stumping for Democrats ahead of midterms
Article Text: US president Trump has been telling voters to view the midterm elections as if he were on the ballot, and on Saturday one of his Democratic predecessors did just that. Days away from the elections that will determine control of the closely divided Congress, Barack Obama took to the campaign trail to accuse the Republican president of corruption, deride his strategy for Iran and skewer the gilded aesthetic he has applied to White House renovations.Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Campaigning in Michigan for US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, Obama framed the Nov 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency. "We got to bring some accountability to this govt," Obama said.Obama, president from 2009 until Trump began his first term in 2017, remains one of the most popular figures among Democrats. They hope that bringing him into the race can fire up their supporters for a tight US Senate race in which El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a former US representative.The former president obliged the Michigan crowd by playing to Democrats' frequently repeated criticisms of Trump and of Republicans' willingness to go along with him. "We have never seen a president excel in straight-up grifting, on your dime, like this," Obama said."Never seen a president so intent on selling favours like this ... Now the party seems to stand for corrupt govt, or inept govt, or no govt."The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. But in a Truth Social post on early Sunday, Trump called Obama a "grossly incompetent President" and labelled El-Sayed a "Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP".Obama also ridiculed the administration's claims of victory against Iran. He argued that the war has given Iran more economic leverage because its threats to attack shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have unsettled oil exporters.In his social media post, Trump derided the Obama administration's approach to the Iranians, saying that he "paid off Iran with $Billions, and gave them a road to a Nuclear Weapon" with his 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action accord with Iran. US withdrew from the 2015 agreement during Trump's first term.He also accused Trump administration of emphasising unimportant matters, sarcastically calling defence secretary Pete Hegseth someone "laser-focused on important matters like the jawline and testosterone levels of troops" and ridiculing White House renovations as tacky. "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory," Obama said.
Article Summary: Obama stumped for Democratic candidates at rallies in Cleveland and Detroit, lampooning the Trump administration. Obama framed the Nov 3 vote as a "circuit breaker" to "at least rein in some of the foolishness" of Trump's presidency. In a social media post on Sunday, Trump called Obama a "grossly incompetent President"

Article Title: In 1973, the Philadelphia Orchestra became the first US orchestra to perform in China; ahead of its 14th China tour, former ambassador David Cohen and his wife pledged $10.5 million to support global
Article Text:
Philadelphia Orchestra marks 14th China tour with $10.5m gift for global tours and new music (Image Credit: The Philadelphia Orchestra)

$10.5 million gift to support cultural diplomacy

From a historic China visit to a continuing diplomatic role

New fund to champion underrepresented composers

Leadership position to carry the Cohens’ names

Ambassador David L Cohen and Rhonda R Cohen President and CEO

Music as a bridge between countries

Music has crossed political borders for decades, and the Philadelphia Orchestra is preparing to continue that tradition with a $10.5 million gift from former US ambassador David L Cohen and his wife, Rhonda R Cohen. According to the orchestra and Ensemble Arts’ official announcement on October 22, 2026, the commitment will support international tours, cultural exchanges and new music. It comes ahead of the orchestra’s 14th visit to China, continuing a relationship that began in 1973, when it became the first American orchestra to perform in the People’s Republic of China. The gift will also support emerging composers and strengthen the organisation’s leadership.The commitment is designed to strengthen the Philadelphia Orchestra’s role as a cultural ambassador through performances and exchanges across national borders. According to the official announcement, the gift will establish the Fund for Cultural Diplomacy, supporting domestic and international tours, residencies, concerts, recordings and educational exchanges.The initiative aims to use music to build relationships between communities and countries, even when diplomatic and political relations face challenges.David Cohen and Rhonda Cohen said they had witnessed how music could build trust and bring people together during their years of public service. The announcement comes as the orchestra prepares to travel to South Korea and China. Its forthcoming Asian tour will combine performances with opportunities for cultural exchange, including engagement with local communities and arts leaders. The funding is intended to help sustain such activities over the longer term.The Philadelphia Orchestra’s relationship with China dates back to 1973, when it became the first American orchestra to perform in the country. More than five decades later, its upcoming visit will be its 14th tour of China, the highest number of such visits by any American orchestra, according to the organisation.The orchestra’s international work has also included performances in Canada. During Cohen’s tenure as US ambassador to Canada from 2021 to 2025, the ensemble toured Montreal, Toronto and Ottawa. In an interview with WHYY, David L Cohen described the goodwill and attention generated by the orchestra’s performances. The experience reinforced his belief that cultural institutions can contribute to international relations in ways that traditional diplomatic engagements may not always achieve.The upcoming tour will open in Incheon, South Korea, on November 5, before continuing to Seoul and then China, where the orchestra is scheduled to perform in Haikou and Beijing, with additional residency activities in Shenzhen and Shanghai. The visit will bring together music, international engagement and opportunities to strengthen cultural connections.Alongside international touring, the donation will support artistic innovation through the creation of the Artistic Innovation and Discovery Fund. Guided by music and artistic director Yannick Nézet-Séguin’s artistic vision, the fund will help the orchestra perform works by overlooked, underrepresented and emerging composers, while also celebrating the contributions of Jewish artists.The initiative aligns with Nézet-Séguin’s efforts to broaden the classical repertoire beyond its established composers. The orchestra has previously championed works by Black American composers Florence Price and William Grant Still. Its recording of Price’s music won a Grammy Award in 2022, bringing renewed attention to a composer whose work had long received less prominence in the classical music world.The new fund is intended to build on such efforts by creating more opportunities for diverse artistic voices to reach audiences through performances and recordings. It will help the orchestra expand its repertoire and bring a wider range of musical perspectives to the concert hall.The $10.5 million commitment will also provide an endowment for the organisation’s top executive position. Ryan Fleur, president and CEO of The Philadelphia Orchestra and Ensemble Arts, will hold the newly named ‘’ position.The naming recognises the couple’s contribution to the institution and their involvement in civic and philanthropic life in Philadelphia. David Cohen previously served as senior adviser to the CEO and senior executive vice-president at Comcast NBCUniversal, and as US ambassador to Canada. Rhonda Cohen is a retired attorney and civic leader who chairs the board of the Glenmede Trust Company and has served on several educational and community organisations.The gift was announced following a major fundraising campaign by the Philadelphia Orchestra and Ensemble Arts that raised $344 million, surpassing its original target of $330 million. The organisation said the campaign proceeds would support operations, maintain venues including the Kimmel Center, Academy of Music and Miller Theater, and strengthen its endowment.The donation comes as the orchestra prepares to return to Asia at a time of international political uncertainty. Its leadership has emphasised that the tour is centred on music, cultural exchange and opportunities to build connections across borders.By combining international performances with educational activities, support for new music and long-term institutional funding, the Cohen gift is intended to extend the orchestra’s work beyond the concert hall. Its historic China tours have helped establish a distinctive role for the ensemble in cultural diplomacy, while the new funds aim to sustain that role for future generations.
Article Summary: Philadelphia Orchestra marks 14th China tour with $10.5m gift for global tours and new music. Former US ambassador David L Cohen and his wife, Rhonda R Cohen, made the gift. It comes ahead of the orchestra’s 14th visit to China, continuing a relationship that began in 1973, when it became the first American orchestra to perform in the country. The donation will also support emerging composers and strengthen the organisation's leadership.

Article Title: Pakistan reopens Iran border after week-long halt to commercial traffic
Article Text:
Following a week-long closure due to security threats, Pakistan has reopened the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing with Iran.

Security concerns preceded reopening

Pakistan has resumed cross-border trade with Iran through a major border point in Balochistan after a seven-day shutdown disrupted cargo movement, left transporters stranded and raised concerns about LPG availability as winter approaches.Commercial traffic restarted on Saturday at the Gabd-Rimdan crossing in Gwadar district, Dawn reported. Officials permitted the movement of import and export consignments carrying consignment notes issued on or before October 16. according to the news agency PTI.Mir Naveed Jan Kalmati, head of the Gwadar chamber of commerce and industry, confirmed that the crossing, also called Gate 250, was operational again.Kalmati said trucks and other vehicles carrying commercial goods were now permitted to travel in both directions between Pakistan and Iran.Welcoming the reopening, he said it would offer relief to traders and transport operators who had been unable to move their cargo during the closure. The restoration of supplies could also help address Pakistan's LPG shortage and ease pressure on rising food and energy costs.The crossing was shut on October 17 by Pakistan's commerce ministry, which did not publicly disclose the reason for the suspension. However, security concerns were believed to have prompted the move.The disruption affected LPG supplies at a time when demand for the fuel generally increases during the colder months.The situation worsened on Thursday when unidentified gunmen attacked trucks parked near the Gabd-Rimdan crossing. Dozens of vehicles were reportedly set ablaze, while several others sustained damage.Local authorities reviewed the security situation before allowing trade to resume on Saturday. Additional security personnel have been deployed to safeguard commercial convoys travelling through the area.The reopening also follows a visit to Iran earlier this week by Pakistan Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, who held discussions with Iranian leaders on bilateral ties and regional developments.Pakistan and Iran share a 909-km frontier between Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province and Pakistan's Balochistan province. The border crossings are vital channels for trade and the movement of goods between the neighbouring countries.
Article Summary: Commercial traffic restarted on Saturday at the Gabd-Rimdan crossing in Gwadar district, Dawn reported. Officials permitted the movement of import and export consignments carrying consignment notes issued on or before October 16. The disruption affected LPG supplies at a time when demand for the fuel generally increases.

Article Title: 'Islamabad arming Afghans to fight anti-Pakistani insurgents': Ex-US envoy sounds alarm
Article Text:
The allegations come amid worsening ties between Islamabad and Kabul

Former US envoy Zalmay Khalilzad has sounded the alarm over reports that Islamabad is recruiting Afghans to fight anti-Pakistan insurgents, warning that relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan are likely to deteriorate further.“There have been many reports that Pakistan is arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan. Now there are reports that the Pakistani military is recruiting Afghans to fight against anti-Pakistan insurgents. As things currently stand, relations between #Afghanistan and #Pakistan are likely to get much worse,” Khalilzad wrote.Pakistan's information ministry on Saturday rejected Khalilzad's allegations as “baseless and misleading”, accusing him of promoting a narrative in support of the Taliban government in Afghanistan.The allegations come amid worsening ties between Islamabad and Kabul, with repeated border clashes and Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan adding to tensions this year.On Saturday, Pakistani forces and Afghan Taliban personnel exchanged fire at several locations along the north-western border. Pakistani security officials and state-run media said troops, backed by artillery, destroyed Taliban posts during hours of fighting in Kurram district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Pakistani officials also claimed that troops killed an unspecified number of Pakistani Taliban militants attempting to cross into Pakistan from eastern Afghanistan. Kabul did not immediately comment on the clashes.Pakistan has accused Afghanistan of providing sanctuary to leaders and fighters of the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which is separate from but closely allied with the Afghan Taliban. Kabul has denied the allegations. The continuing violence has further strained relations between the two countries.
Article Summary: Zalmay Khalilzad warns that relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan are likely to deteriorate further. The allegations come amid worsening ties between Islamabad and Kabul. On Saturday, Pakistani forces and Afghan Taliban personnel exchanged fire at several locations along the north-western border.

Article Title: 'Pak defeated, cannot fight us': Baloch rebels launch fresh strike; several killed
Article Text:
The group also claimed to have taken control of the Muzhani police station

The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a series of strikes against Pakistani security forces, alleging that its fighters killed a Military Intelligence (MI) captain and several personnel of the Pakistan Army’s Special Services Group (SSG) during its ongoing Operation Almas.In a press release issued by its spokesperson, Major Gwahram Baloch, the separatist group claimed that Pakistani forces had suffered significant human and material losses at multiple locations and were forced to retreat following clashes. The BLF, as cited by news agency ANI said that the operation was continuing on several fronts with “full intensity and success”.Videos purportedly showing the ongoing violence have also surfaced. In one clip, a woman is heard saying, “Pakistan is defeated now & and cannot fight us”, as gunfire continues in the background. Another video showed a woman firing what appeared to be an assault rifle.The BLF further claimed that its fighters had overrun the main camp of the Frontier Works Organization (FWO) and hoisted the organisation’s flag at Gwadar Zero Point, describing the development as evidence of its advances during the operation.The group also claimed to have taken control of the Muzhani police station, seizing official weapons and military equipment. It alleged that a police official was killed during the confrontation.In a separate incident in Gubd, the BLF said its fighters attacked a convoy of Pakistani security forces, destroying an army vehicle and killing or injuring several personnel travelling in it. The group also claimed that its fighters had taken control of the police checkpoint at Gubd Cross.
Article Summary: The Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) has claimed responsibility for a series of strikes against Pakistani security forces. The group alleges that its fighters killed a Military Intelligence (MI) captain and several personnel of the Pakistan Army’s Special Services Group (SSG)

Article Title: Pakistan's elite want out? Khawaja Asif flags bureaucrats' alleged exit plans to foreign shores
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan defence minister Khwaja Asif

Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif has questioned the loyalty of senior bureaucrats, alleging that several government officials planned to settle abroad while serving the country, according to a report by Pakistan's Express Tribune.In a post on X, Asif said Pakistan had capable and honest bureaucrats, but alleged that many officials had made Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and other European countries their permanent homes over the past several years.He claimed some officers had prepared for their relocation under a deliberate plan while employed by the Pakistani government. Portugal, he said, had emerged as a destination for what he described as a bureaucratic exodus in recent years. He added that he had raised the issue on social media a few months ago.Asif said the officers whose names had surfaced in connection with the matter had held important positions and remained close to successive governments. He also alleged that an individual who facilitated permanent residency arrangements had fled after collecting substantial sums of money from several influential bureaucrats.The minister did not identify the officials or provide details to substantiate the allegations. He said troubling accounts were circulating about the matter and questioned whether senior officials who had enjoyed the privileges and respect associated with public service had remained committed to Pakistan.“Does it rise above all doubt and suspicion, or are they merely in transit?” Asif asked, questioning whether such officials viewed Pakistan as their permanent home or merely a temporary stop before settling abroad.
Article Summary: Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif has questioned the loyalty of senior bureaucrats. He alleges that several government officials planned to settle abroad while serving the country. Portugal has emerged as a destination for what he described as a bureaucratic exodus in recent years. He also alleged that an individual who facilitated permanent residency arrangements had fled.

Article Title: Pakistan army officer killed in IED blast during Balochistan operation
Article Text:
Pakistan Army major killed in Balochistan IED blast as security forces eliminate four terrorists.

A Pakistan Army major was killed in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast during a security operation in Balochistan province, while security forces killed four terrorists in a separate operation, the military said on Monday.According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the military's media wing, security forces conducted operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Gwadar and Jattakabad in Kalat district on Sunday following reports of terrorist presence.During an operation in Jattakabad, the forces killed four terrorists and recovered “a large cache of arms and ammunition”, the Army said.In a separate action, security forces carried out clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni in Gwadar district. During the operation, 34-year-old Major Wajahat Waheed was killed in an IED attack while leading the operation.“Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area,” the Army said.The military added that security forces and law enforcement agencies remained committed to eliminating foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism in the country.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for killing the four terrorists and expressed grief over the death of the officer.“Major Wajahat Waheed sacrificed his life for the protection of our beloved homeland; the nation is proud of its brave son,” the prime minister said.Sharif also extended condolences to the officer's family and prayed for the elevation of his rank.Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, with security forces continuing operations to contain the violence.A day earlier, security forces killed eight terrorists during operations in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Pakistan Army major killed in Balochistan IED blast as security forces eliminate four terrorists. Major Wajahat Waheed was killed in an IED attack while leading the operation. Security forces carried out clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni in Gwadar district.

Article Title: US-designated LeT terrorist dies after mysteriously falling from building in Lahore
Article Text:
LeT terrorist Chaudhary Muhammed Sarwar.

NEW DELHI: US designated Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar alias Abu Hashim, one of the founding members of the outfit, died after mysteriously falling from the fourth floor of Markaz Qudesia in Lahore Sunday.The incident reminded of a similar death that had occurred in 2016 when fake currency kingpin, Javed Khanani, had died after falling from an under construction building in Karachi.Sarwar was currently handling the finance wing and fundraising excercise in Punjab province under the garb of the outfit's political wing, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League. He was a close aide of both Hafiz Saeed and current deputy chief Saifullah Kasuri. Sarwar's son had also died in a road accident a few months ago.It was in 2016 tha Sarwar was designated a terrorist by the US justice department who termed himself as a senior LeT memeber in Lahore active since early 2000s, holding various leadership roles in the group. At the time, he was LeT’s emir for Lahore, a position he has held since at least January 2015."As the LeT emir of Lahore, Sarwar maintains relationships with LeT’s most senior leaders. Between 2012 and 2013, Sarwar worked with LeT’s foreign affairs chief Hafiz Abdul Rahman Makki, and in early 2013, Makki asked Sarwar for money to pay for his travel within Pakistan," the US justice department had said in its statement."Sarwar had been directly involved in LeT fundraising activities and used the formal financial system in Pakistan to raise and move funds on behalf of LeT. For example, in 2008, Sarwar led delegations of businessmen to LeT facilities for the purpose of soliciting donations for the group," it added.
Article Summary: US designated Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Chaudhry Mohammad Sarwar alias Abu Hashim died after mysteriously falling from the fourth floor of Markaz Qudesia in Lahore Sunday. Sarwar was currently handling the finance wing and fundraising excercise in Punjab province under the garb of the outfit's political wing, Pakistan Markazi Muslim League.

Article Title: Pakistani forces kill 8 militants in Balochistan, raid hideouts as abductions rise
Article Text:
The operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas (Photo: ANI).

Pakistani security forces on Sunday reportedly killed eight militants in three intelligence-led operations across districts of Balochistan province, amid rising cases of abduction in the troubled region.The operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas, according to the Inter Service Public Relations (ISPR), the media wing of the Pakistan Army.In the Panjpai area of Quetta district, terrorists trying to set up a roadblock to disrupt local traffic were "intercepted by security forces, resulting in [the] killing of five terrorists", the ISPR said in a statement.In Nushki district, security forces stormed a hideout, and two terrorists were killed in an intense exchange of fire, the army said. Around 500 kilograms of explosives were also recovered from the terrorists during that operation. In Khuzdar district, one terrorist was killed, the ISPR added.Balochistan, which borders Afghanistan, has seen a surge in abductions and attacks on civilians and securityforces in recent years, prompting the government to step up its anti-militant operations.On Saturday, unidentified armed men hijacked a bus carrying 20 trainee police officers near Mastung, on the Quetta-Karachi highway, and took them away. Their whereabouts remain unknown.On Sunday, at least 18 workers were abducted, and another was injured when unidentified armed men attacked a marble mining site in the province. The incident happened early in the morning in the remote Naal area of Khuzdar district, police said. The attackers arrived on motorcycles and other vehicles and stormed the site.According to PTI, no insurgent group or individual has claimed responsibility for the attack.The police and the provincial government have yet to confirm the incident officially, but two police officers, speaking on condition of anonymity, said 18 workers had been taken away by the attackers. PTI reported."They came on bikes and vehicles and opened fire and then rounded up the workers present at the site and abducted 18 of them before fleeing," a police officer said.Most of those abducted came from nearby villages and areas, he added, and another worker was injured in the attack.
Article Summary: Pakistani security forces reportedly kill eight militants in three intelligence- led operations across districts of Balochistan province. Operations took place on Saturday in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts, following intelligence that the militants were hiding in those areas. On Saturday, unidentified armed men hijacked a bus carrying 20 trainee police officers.

Article Title: Pakistan’s decades of backing terror comes full circle as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa falls under emergency rule
Article Text:
The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers. In the affected districts, the constitutional distinction between judicial and executive authority has reportedly been set aside, concentrating control in unelected hands.

Decades of militant policy and blowback

Emergency rule and the erosion of elected authority

Opposition crackdown deepens rights concerns

Tribal communities face renewed uncertainty

Pakistan’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11 has placed the province under direct federal control. It has effectively suspended the regional administration led by imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).The move, which invokes Articles 232 and 234 of the Pakistani Constitution, comes amid a worsening security situation and a crackdown on opposition leaders and protesters. It has also renewed questions over Pakistan’s decades-long policy of using militant groups for strategic gains. A report by news agency ANI highlights how this policy has fuelled the violence now threatening its own territory.The emergency has extended federal control across 12 districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, further weakening elected authority in a province that has long borne the consequences of Pakistan’s security policies. The move follows years of political turmoil, including Khan’s imprisonment, constitutional amendments that have weakened judicial independence, and the removal of the PTI-led provincial government.The concentration of power in unelected authorities, alongside the military’s expanding role in civilian affairs, has raised concerns over the state of democracy in Pakistan, according to a report by news agency ANI.Pakistan’s security crisis has deep roots in its long-standing use of militant groups as instruments of state policy. For more than five decades, the country has pursued strategic depth through its relationship with armed groups, while distinguishing between factions considered useful and those viewed as threats.This approach has contributed to a cycle of violence that has increasingly turned inward.As stated in the report, the state has repeatedly shifted its position towards militant organisations, including groups hostile to its own security forces. During former army chief General Qamar Javed Bajwa’s tenure, cadres of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) were relocated to parts of the erstwhile Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The consequences have proved difficult to contain. Pakistan’s struggle with militancy has exposed the risks of treating armed groups as strategic assets while assuming their violence can be directed towards selected targets.Former US secretary of state Hillary Clinton captured this danger in a widely cited remark, “one cannot rear snakes in a backyard and expect them to bite only neighbours, as they will eventually turn on their keepers”.Rather than confronting the broader implications of this policy, Pakistan has continued to differentiate between militant factions it considers acceptable and those it seeks to eliminate. The resulting security failures have placed civilians, particularly in the tribal areas, at the centre of a prolonged conflict.The imposition of emergency rule marks another stage in the concentration of power within Pakistan’s security establishment. The federal intervention has effectively displaced the PTI-led provincial administration, depriving the opposition of its remaining provincial government.The move follows Khan’s incarceration and constitutional changes that have curtailed judicial independence and shielded military leadership from accountability. Critics argue that these developments have weakened the institutions meant to limit executive and military power.The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers. In the affected districts, the constitutional distinction between judicial and executive authority has reportedly been set aside, concentrating control in unelected hands.Instead of addressing the failures behind the province’s deteriorating security situation, authorities have expanded federal and military involvement in civilian administration. The move has intensified concerns that emergency powers are being used not only to manage the security crisis but also to consolidate political control.The intervention has been accompanied by a wider crackdown on the opposition. Leaders and legislators have been detained, residences raided and political demonstrations suppressed. Protesters have faced police firing, tear gas and mass arrests.The treatment of political opponents has fuelled concerns that dissent is increasingly being treated as a security threat. The use of force against protesters has also raised questions about the government’s claim that extraordinary measures are needed to restore law and order.The crackdown comes amid concerns over restrictions on reporting from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, following earlier developments in Khyber before a blanket media ban was imposed on events in the province. Such restrictions risk limiting public scrutiny of security operations and their impact on civilians.The growing concentration of authority has therefore created a parallel crisis. While the state faces a persistent militant threat, its response has further narrowed the space for political opposition and public dissent.The latest intervention has also placed additional pressure on communities that have endured years of displacement and insecurity. Past military operations, including Zarb-e-Azb and Radd-ul-Fasad, remain associated with civilian hardship and human rights concerns.Thousands of displaced families are still awaiting return and rehabilitation. For these communities, the emergency raises fears of another period of disruption, particularly as the authorities expand their control and military involvement in civilian affairs.The consequences of Pakistan’s security policies have thus extended beyond the fight against armed groups. Tribal populations have faced displacement, civilian casualties and prolonged instability, while the failure to resolve the underlying conflict has left many vulnerable to further intervention.The emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa brings these tensions into sharper focus. A state that has long relied on militant groups to pursue strategic objectives now faces the consequences of violence within its own borders. Its response, however, has centred on expanding federal control, weakening elected authority and restricting opposition activity.Rather than resolving the crisis, the latest measures risk deepening the divide between the state and the communities it claims to protect. The removal of an elected provincial government, the concentration of power in unelected institutions and the crackdown on dissent point to a broader struggle over Pakistan’s democratic future, even as the country confronts the long-term fallout of its militant policies.
Article Summary: Emergency has extended federal control across 12 districts in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It has effectively suspended the regional administration led by Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) It comes amid a worsening security situation and a crackdown on opposition leaders and protesters. The emergency has also raised concerns about the separation of powers.

Article Title: Pakistan plans Moon landing by 2035, expands space cooperation with China
Article Text:
Pakistan sets 2035 Moon landing target as space programme expands, minister says (representative image)

First Pakistani astronaut to travel to China’s space station

Pakistan-China cooperation extends to lunar exploration

Space education and proposed museum

India’s space roadmap: From Gaganyaan to a Moon landing

Pakistan aims to land on the Moon by 2035 as it expands its space programme, planning minister Ahsan Iqbal said on Sunday, announcing that the country's first astronaut would embark on a space mission from China on November 25.Addressing the concluding ceremony of World Space Week 2026 in Narowal district of Punjab province, Iqbal said cooperation with China would help Pakistan advance its space exploration ambitions.Pakistan’s “first astronaut will embark on a space mission from China’s space centre on November 25, while the country aims to achieve a lunar landing by 2035,” he said, according to news agency PTI.The minister highlighted the growing role of space technology in agriculture, communications, climate monitoring, education and national security. He stressed that scientific research and space exploration were important for technological advancement.The upcoming mission is part of wider cooperation between Pakistan and China in space science and technology. According to Reuters, two Pakistani candidates, pilots Khurram Daud and Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, have been undergoing training in China, with one expected to be selected for the flight.The selected astronaut will serve as a payload specialist aboard China's Tiangong space station, conducting scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft, Reuters reported last month.Pakistan's space agency, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), signed an agreement with the China Manned Space Agency in February 2025 to prepare a Pakistani astronaut for the mission, according to The Express Tribune.The two candidates had been training at the China Astronaut Research and Training Centre in Beijing, learning spacecraft systems, Mandarin and the physical demands of spaceflight.The mission is expected to last about a week. The astronaut will travel aboard a Chinese spacecraft launched from China and return to Earth with members of a Chinese crew.Pakistan does not have an independent launch vehicle or crewed spacecraft, making the mission dependent on China's space infrastructure and training facilities.Beyond the human spaceflight programme, Pakistan and China are collaborating on a Pakistani-built lunar rover planned for China's Chang'e-8 mission, expected around 2028.The rover is intended to use artificial intelligence-based stereo imaging to identify obstacles, assess distances and navigate the lunar surface autonomously, as direct real-time control from Earth would not be possible.However, Pakistan's participation in the lunar rover project is separate from its stated ambition to land on the Moon by 2035.According to Reuters, a Pakistani space agency official last month had said there was no official commitment or discussion about sending a Pakistani astronaut to the Moon under the existing partnership.Iqbal was speaking at the conclusion of World Space Week 2026, which was celebrated in Narowal for the first time in collaboration with SUPARCO. The event aimed to raise awareness among young people about space science, scientific research and modern technology.The minister also announced plans to establish Pakistan's first Space Museum at the University of Narowal to promote scientific awareness and encourage students to pursue careers in space science and technology.He said improved access to higher education was allowing students who had previously faced financial barriers to perform well academically.Iqbal congratulated the University of Narowal on securing first position at the Islamabad Science Festival, saying the achievement reflected the talent and potential of Pakistan's youth.The minister said the proposed museum would further encourage young people to explore scientific fields and pursue opportunities in space research and technology.India has also been advancing its space programme, with plans to send astronauts into orbit, establish its own space station and land an Indian on the Moon by 2040.According to the Union government’s roadmap outlined in Parliament in August, the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission, carrying the humanoid robot Vyommitra, is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026. Two further uncrewed missions are planned before India attempts its first crewed orbital flight, targeted by 2027.India also plans to establish the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035. The proposed station will comprise five modules, with the development and launch of its first module already approved.The longer-term goal is to send an Indian astronaut to the Moon by 2040.Other planned missions include Chandrayaan-4, which is intended to demonstrate technologies for returning lunar samples to Earth, and a Venus Orbiter Mission to study the planet’s surface, subsurface and atmosphere.These projects form part of India’s broader Space Vision 2047, which aims to expand its human spaceflight capabilities and deepen its role in space exploration.
Article Summary: Pakistan's first astronaut will embark on a space mission from China on November 25. Ahsan Iqbal said cooperation with China would help Pakistan advance its space exploration ambitions. Pakistan and China are collaborating on a Pakistani-built lunar rover planned for China's Chang'e-8 mission, expected around 2028.

Article Title: Balochistan unrest: Teacher's killing sparks outrage, kin say Pak officials shielding 'death squads'
Article Text:
What are Balochistan's 'death squads'?

(With ANI inputs)

The alleged torture and killing of a teacher in Pakistan’s restive Balochistan province triggered protests by his family members and local residents, who warned that a key highway would be blockaded if authorities failed to take action.The protesters accused Pakistani forces of shielding those allegedly responsible for the death of Parvez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, The Balochistan Post reported.According to Mazar’s relatives, he was "taken away" in front of his family on Tuesday and was found dead the following day. They claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.Protesters, including Mazar’s children, gathered outside the Pasni Press Club, demanding the immediate arrest of those responsible for his death. They demanded accountability and justice for the deceased teacher's family.The demonstrators warned that failure to address their demands would prompt them to stage a sit-in at Pasni Zero Point and block the Makran Coastal Highway, a key route connecting Gwadar with Karachi in Sindh province, Pakistan’s largest city and the country's financial and commercial hub.They demanded that state institutions take action against armed groups accused of abducting, torturing and killing civilians while allegedly operating under the protection of state agencies.Baloch rights organisations and activists use the term “death squads” to describe armed groups they allege receive support or protection from Pakistani state institutions.These groups have been accused of targeting civilians, political activists and human rights defenders in Balochistan, a province long affected by an insurgency and a security crackdown.
Article Summary: Pervez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, was found dead the following day. His family claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.

Article Title: Strong 6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan

6.0-magnitude quake strikes Balochistan in Pakistan

More details awaited
